mainTopic: What exactly do רבי חייא and בר קפרא disagree about, and how can each explain the other's sworn report of what רבי taught?
overview: The גמרא wants to find the principle behind the argument between רבי חייא (two counts) and בר קפרא (one count). First it suggests they argue about איסור כולל according to רבי יוסי. That fails for מליקה, where both איסורים start at the same moment. So the גמרא says they argue about איסור בבת אחת, two איסורים that begin together. It then rereads the זר and בעל מום cases so that both איסורים begin at once: a boy who became an adult at that moment, or a cut with a טמא knife. Next the גמרא looks at the oaths each of them swore about what רבי taught. If the argument is according to רבי יוסי, בר קפרא would have to call רבי חייא a liar. So the גמרא moves the argument to רבי שמעון, but then בר קפרא's oath seems pointless, and the גמרא calls that a קשיא. It also asks how רבי חייא could explain בר קפרא's version, and begins to answer that רבי taught בר קפרא two cases of exemption.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle lies behind the argument between רבי חייא and בר קפרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what idea is really behind the argument between רבי חייא and בר קפרא. This is a setup question, and the next step offers a first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the bottom line: רבי חייא says two counts and בר קפרא says one. Now the גמרא wants the principle that produces these two results, so the argument is not just a list of cases.

keyTerms.meaning: In what do they disagree? The standard way to ask for the root of an argument.

phrases.english: In what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" are רבי חייא and בר קפרא, from the cases discussed just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of the earlier argument between רבי חייא and בר קפרא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that splits רבי חייא from בר קפרא.

steps.title: First suggestion: they argue about איסור כולל according to רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion is that they argue about איסור כולל in רבי יוסי's view. רבי חייא says רבי יוסי lets it take effect, so there are two counts. בר קפרא says it does not take effect, so there is only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about a more inclusive prohibition, according to רבי יוסי. רבי חייא holds that, in רבי יוסי's view, one is liable twice for an איסור כולל. בר קפרא holds one is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the argument is about איסור כולל, a second איסור that falls on top of an existing one because it is wider. They argue whether רבי יוסי lets an איסור כולל take effect. If it does, there are two counts; if not, only one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key move is that both sides say they are explaining רבי יוסי. The question is whether, in his view, the second איסור takes effect and adds a second count (רבי חייא), or does not take effect, so the person is liable only once (בר קפרא).

keyTerms.meaning: A wider איסור that also covers things that were not forbidden before, so it can fall on top of an earlier איסור.
According to the view of.
He is liable on two counts.
He is liable on only one count.

phrases.english: About a more inclusive prohibition,
and according to Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Ḥiyya holds:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּאִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל מִיחַיַּיב תַּרְתֵּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei holds that with a more inclusive prohibition, one is liable twice,
Bar Kappara holds:
one is liable only once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with a first proposal.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is about how many counts רבי יוסי gives for an איסור כולל.

steps.title: Where is the איסור כולל? It works for the זר and the בעל מום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where an איסור כולל appears in these cases. It grants that the idea fits the זר on שבת and the טמא בעל מום, since in each one a wider איסור came on top of an existing one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what more inclusive prohibition is there here? Granted with a non-priest: at first he was allowed to do work and forbidden in the Temple service. Then שבת came, and since he became forbidden to do work, he also became forbidden in the service. A blemished priest: at first he was allowed to eat holy food and forbidden in the service. He became טמא, and since he became forbidden to eat, he also became forbidden in the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to test the suggestion by checking each case. It shows that the זר and the בעל מום really do fit איסור כולל. This sets up the problem case that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the זר, the איסור of serving existed first, and שבת brought a wider איסור of מלאכה that also covers the עבודה. For the בעל מום, the איסור of serving existed first, and טומאה brought a wider איסור that also covers eating. In both cases the second איסור came later and was wider, which is exactly an איסור כולל.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this works. It sets up a contrast with a case that will not work.
At first, originally.
Work that is forbidden on שבת.
The service in the בית המקדש.
Since, because. Here: since it already forbids one thing, it also forbids the other.
A כהן with a physical blemish, who may not serve.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not yet the challenge itself. The בשלמא part only grants that two cases fit; the real question comes in the next step with מליקה.

phrases.english: And what more inclusive prohibition is there here?
Granted with a non-priest:
At first he was permitted to do work
and forbidden in the Temple service.
Then שבת came,
since he became forbidden to do work,
he also became forbidden in the service.
A blemished priest:
At first he was permitted to eat,
phrases.notes: He means eating holy food, which a blemished כהן may still eat.

phrases.english: and forbidden in the service.
He became ritually impure,
since he became forbidden to eat,
he also became forbidden in the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי אִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל אִיכָּא הָכָא? בִּשְׁלָמָא זָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the proposal of step 2 against the actual cases, starting with the ones that fit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proposal that the argument is about איסור כולל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גמרא checks whether every case in the argument contains an איסור כולל. Here it grants the two cases that do.

steps.title: מליקה does not fit איסור כולל
steps.stepSummary: In מליקה both איסורים start at the same moment, so there is no איסור כולל, and the first suggestion fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But מליקה is found only at once; you cannot find it as a more inclusive prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the actual challenge: the case of מליקה does not have an איסור כולל, because both איסורים begin together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איסור כולל needs a first איסור already in place and a wider one that comes later. With a bird killed by מליקה, the איסור for a זר and the איסור of נבלה begin at the same moment, so nothing came first. Since רבי חייא and בר קפרא argue about this case too, איסור כולל cannot be the root of their argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Killing a bird offering by pinching its neck with the fingernail.
At the same moment, simultaneously.
You find it, you can picture it this way.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that an איסור כולל, where one איסור comes first and a wider one comes later, is a different idea from an איסור בבת אחת, where two איסורים start together.

phrases.english: But a bird killed by pinching —
it is found only at the same moment,
you cannot find it as a more inclusive prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא structure of step 3 by bringing the case that does not fit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proposal of step 2 that the argument is about איסור כולל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In מליקה both איסורים start together, so no איסור כולל exists, yet the two sides argue about this case too.

steps.title: New explanation: they argue about איסור בבת אחת according to רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops איסור כולל and says instead that they argue about two איסורים that start together, according to רבי יוסי. רבי חייא says two counts and בר קפרא says one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they disagree about a prohibition that takes effect at once, according to רבי יוסי. רבי חייא holds that, in רבי יוסי's view, for an איסור that takes effect at once, one is liable twice. בר קפרא holds one is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces its first answer. The argument is now about איסור בבת אחת, which clearly fits מליקה. The next step asks whether it fits the other two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea covers מליקה, where both איסורים start together. Whether it also fits the זר and the בעל מום, where one איסור seemed to come first, is the challenge raised in step 6. The setup stays the same: both sides explain רבי יוסי, and only the type of איסור has changed from כולל to בבת אחת.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Here it rejects the earlier answer and brings a new one.
Two איסורים that take effect at the same moment.

steps.whatToRemember: Second explanation: רבי חייא and בר קפרא both follow רבי יוסי and argue about איסור בבת אחת. רבי חייא says he gives two counts, and בר קפרא says only one. The first explanation, איסור כולל, was dropped because of מליקה. This is not the last word: step 6 tests it against the cases, and step 9 attacks it, which leads the גמרא to move the argument to רבי שמעון in step 10.

phrases.english: Rather, they disagree about a prohibition that takes effect at once,
and according to Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Ḥiyya holds:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּאִיסּוּר בַּת אַחַת מִיחַיַּיב תַּרְתֵּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei holds that with a prohibition that takes effect at once, one is liable twice,
and Bar Kappara holds:
one is liable only once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation of step 2 after the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They argue about איסור כולל according to רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about איסור בבת אחת according to רבי יוסי, which also fits מליקה.

steps.title: Where is the simultaneous איסור in these cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer. In the cases of the זר on שבת and the טמא בעל מום, the איסורים seem to come one after the other, not at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, in these cases, where is there a prohibition that starts all at once?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the answer from step 5. That answer said the argument is about איסורים that start together, but two of the three cases do not look that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 said the זר on שבת and the טמא בעל מום fit איסור כולל, because one איסור came on top of an earlier one. If the איסורים came one after the other, the new explanation about איסור בת אחת does not seem to fit them. Only מליקה clearly fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Two prohibitions that start at the very same moment
But here, in these cases

phrases.english: But here, what simultaneous prohibition
is there here?
phrases.notes: "Here" means the זר on שבת and the טמא בעל מום, where one איסור seemed to come before the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא, מַאי אִיסּוּר בַּת אַחַת אִיכָּא הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 5's claim that all the cases are איסור בת אחת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 5 that the dispute is about איסורים that start together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The זר and בעל מום cases look like one איסור following another, so they do not fit the simultaneous model.

steps.title: The זר who became an adult on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The זר case can be simultaneous: a boy became an adult on שבת. At that moment the איסור of זרות and the איסור of שבת both start for him together.
steps.simpleTranslation: A זר who did the עבודה on שבת: for example, he grew two hairs on שבת, so זרות and שבת came on him at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge for the first case. It shows how the זר on שבת can be a case of two איסורים starting together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child is not obligated in מצוות, so no איסור applies to him yet. If he becomes an adult on שבת itself, both איסורים begin together at the same moment. So the case can fit איסור בת אחת.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hairs, the sign that a boy has become an adult
The איסור on a non-כהן doing the עבודה
Together, at the same time

phrases.english: A non-priest who served on Shabbat:
for example, where he grew two hairs on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: Before this he was a child and not obligated, so no איסור applied to him yet.

phrases.english: so that being a non-priest and Shabbat apply to him
together.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָר שֶׁשִּׁימֵּשׁ בְּשַׁבָּת כְּגוֹן דְּאַיְיתִי שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6's challenge for the זר case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) so both איסורים start at once.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זר was already an adult, so שבת came on top of an existing איסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The boy became an adult on שבת, so both איסורים began at the same moment.

steps.title: The בעל מום who became טמא at the same moment
steps.stepSummary: The בעל מום case can also be simultaneous. Either he became an adult and became טמא at that same moment, or he cut off his finger with a טמא knife, so the מום and the טומאה came together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The בעל מום too: for example, he grew two hairs and became טמא, so being a בעל מום and טומאה came on him together. Or, he cut off his finger with a טמא knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by doing the same thing for the second case. It gives two ways the בעל מום and the טומאה could start at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one uses the same trick as the זר case: the איסורים begin when he becomes an adult. Option two works even for an adult: one cut with a טמא knife makes him a בעל מום and טמא in the very same instant.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן with a physical blemish, who may not do the עבודה
Became ritually impure
Alternatively
A ritually impure knife

phrases.english: A blemished one as well:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן דְּאַיְיתִי שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת וְאִיטַּמִּי לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: for example, where he grew two hairs and became impure,
so that being blemished and impurity apply to him
together.
Alternatively, where he cut off his finger
with an impure knife.
phrases.notes: The same cut gives him the מום and makes him טמא, both in one moment.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Continuation of the תירוץ in step 7
steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל מוּם נָמֵי כְּגוֹן דְּאַיְיתִי שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת וְאִיטַּמִּי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of answer as step 7 to the second case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case, with two possible scenarios.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן was already a בעל מום before he became טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מום and the טומאה started at the same moment, either when he became an adult or through one cut with a טמא knife.
steps.whatToRemember: All three cases (זר on שבת, טמא בעל מום, מליקה) can now be read as איסור בת אחת, two איסורים starting together.

steps.title: Would בר קפרא say that רבי חייא swore falsely?
steps.stepSummary: If the argument is according to רבי יוסי, רבי חייא can explain בר קפרא's version: רבי taught it to him according to רבי שמעון. But בר קפרא has no opinion that gives two counts, so he would have to say רבי חייא was lying.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for רבי חייא: when רבי taught him, it was according to רבי יוסי, and when he taught בר קפרא, it was according to רבי שמעון. But according to בר קפרא, was רבי חייא simply telling a lie?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with saying the argument is according to רבי יוסי. Each of them swore he heard his version from רבי, and בר קפרא would have no way to explain רבי חייא's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא can say both versions came from רבי, each according to a different תנא: two counts by רבי יוסי, one count by רבי שמעון. בר קפרא holds that even רבי יוסי gives only one count, and רבי שמעון surely gives no more. So no תנא gives two, and בר קפרא would have to call רבי חייא a liar, which is unthinkable.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out fine for, granted
He (רבי) taught him
According to the opinion of
Is he simply telling a lie?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is with רבי חייא's view. His side works fine. The problem is only with how בר קפרא could explain רבי חייא's sworn version.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Ḥiyya,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אַתְנְיֵיהּ לְדִידֵיהּ — אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: when he taught him, it was according to Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי, the teacher both of them say they heard it from.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אַתְנְיֵיהּ לְבַר קַפָּרָא — אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: when he taught bar Kappara, it was according to Rabbi Shimon.
But according to bar Kappara,
was Rabbi Ḥiyya telling a lie?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא כִּי אַתְנְיֵיהּ לְדִידֵיהּ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the case problem solved, the גמרא attacks step 5's explanation from a different side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that they argue about איסור בת אחת according to רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that explanation no תנא gives two counts in בר קפרא's eyes, so he would have to say רבי חייא swore falsely.

steps.title: They argue about simultaneous איסורים according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves the argument to רבי שמעון. They argue about איסורים that start together according to רבי שמעון: רבי חייא says even רבי שמעון gives two counts there, and בר קפרא says one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they argue about a simultaneous איסור, and according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation to escape the problem in step 9. It keeps the idea of איסור בת אחת but places the argument within רבי שמעון's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון usually holds that one איסור cannot take effect on another. The question is whether he agrees when both start together. רבי חייא says yes, so two counts. בר קפרא says no, so one count. This removes the problem of step 9, but steps 11 and 12 raise new problems with this explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: They argue about

phrases.english: Rather, they disagree about a simultaneous prohibition,
and according to Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא קָמִיפַּלְגִי בְּאִיסּוּר בַּת אַחַת וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces step 5 because of the problem raised in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the argument to a different תנא's opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They argued according to רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue according to רבי שמעון: does he agree that איסורים starting together both take effect?

steps.title: Why would בר קפרא need to swear?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא's oath makes sense, because he was saying something surprising about רבי שמעון. But בר קפרא's view is what everyone already assumed about רבי שמעון, so why did he need to swear? The גמרא leaves this as a קשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for רבי חייא: he swore to take רבי שמעון away from his usual assumed position. But according to בר קפרא, why did he need to swear? This is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new explanation from step 10 and finds no answer. It ends with the word קשיא, meaning the problem stays unsolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows רבי שמעון says one איסור does not take effect on another, so one count is the expected answer. רבי חייא was saying something new, two counts even by רבי שמעון, so an oath gives it force. בר קפרא was only saying the expected thing, so an oath seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Swears, takes an oath
To take out of, to exclude
From his usual assumed position
It is difficult; the question stays unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: Explaining the argument by רבי יוסי makes בר קפרא call רבי חייא a liar. Explaining it by רבי שמעון makes בר קפרא's oath pointless, and the גמרא marks this point with קשיא. The discussion still continues in step 12.
steps.confusionAlert: Here קשיא is not a new question. It is the גמרא admitting that this explanation has a problem with no answer.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Ḥiyya,

phrases.aramaic: קָא מִישְׁתְּבַע לְאַפּוֹקֵי לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מֵחֶזְקֵיהּ.
phrases.english: he swears in order to take Rabbi Shimon out of his presumed position.
phrases.notes: Everyone assumed רבי שמעון never lets one איסור take effect on another, so רבי חייא's two counts were a surprise.

phrases.english: But according to bar Kappara,
why did he need to swear?
It is difficult.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בר קפרא's view matches the usual assumption about רבי שמעון, so his oath would add nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the גמרא reading even the oaths of the חכמים as clues to their real views. The final word קשיא tells us this explanation was never fully saved.

steps.title: How can רבי חייא explain בר קפרא's version?
steps.stepSummary: Under the version where they argue about רבי שמעון, בר קפרא can explain רבי חייא's 'two counts' as רבי teaching him רבי יוסי's view. רבי חייא, however, seems to have no way to explain בר קפרא's 'one count'. Was בר קפרא lying?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for בר קפרא: when רבי taught him, it was according to רבי שמעון, and when רבי taught רבי חייא, it was according to רבי יוסי. But according to רבי חייא, was בר קפרא lying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another problem with the idea that the argument is about רבי שמעון. בר קפרא has an easy way to explain where רבי חייא's version came from, but רבי חייא seems to have none for בר קפרא's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side swore that this is what רבי taught him, so each side needs an honest way to explain the other's report. בר קפרא can say רבי taught רבי חייא according to רבי יוסי, who gives two counts. רבי חייא holds that even רבי שמעון gives two counts when the איסורים start together, so no one would give one count, and בר קפרא would have to be lying.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sides swore to what they heard from רבי. רבי חייא holds that both רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון give two counts when the איסורים start together, so no teaching would produce 'one count'. That would make בר קפרא a liar.

steps.title: רבי taught בר קפרא two cases of exemption
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers that רבי taught בר קפרא two specific cases where the person is exempt from a second count. This is how בר קפרא came to report 'one count' honestly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא can tell you: when רבי taught בר קפרא, he taught him two cases of exemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי חייא's answer, so that בר קפרא was not lying. רבי really did teach him about being exempt, but only in two particular cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'two' are the two cases discussed earlier: the זר who served on שבת and the טמא בעל מום who served. רבי taught that in these two cases there is only one count. These words show that בר קפרא's 'one count' came from a real teaching of רבי, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
